coverage: all 12 public protocol descriptors have an XState implementation with the catalog principal states
scope abort is exactly-once, stale actor identities are rejected, and injected-clock traces are bounded
drag and resize cancellation, capture loss, wrong-pointer handling, and revision conflicts leave no residual actor state
resize delivery switches between live, throttled, deferred, and adaptive policies
motion leases finish, cancel, skip, and dispose queued/running driver resources exactly once
replace and retarget interruption policies sample current visual properties before continuing
unsupported, skipped, failed, and disposed View Transitions commit semantic state once and fall back progressively
load planning drops decoration before spatial continuity and never degrades direct input tracking
limitations: The catalog/state checks do not constitute exhaustive generated transition, timeout, and recovery-path coverage.
JSDOM and deterministic driver tests do not measure the one-CSS-pixel re-grab target or real browser duplicate-name behavior.
The run contains no physical 60 Hz or 120 Hz latency, heap, resource, or assistive-technology evidence.
